Subject: Optimize Toolkit — post-workshop pricing model and quant/cache guidance

Hey Peter — thanks again for the workshop this morning. Good discussion; I summarized the pricing/packaging options we sketched and a few proposals for the pilot. Please find the deck and cost scenarios attached. Quick TL;DR up front:

- Pilot scope: 3 routes for ingestion + 15k monthly active inference sessions (avg 180 tokens/session)
- Recommended technical levers: 8-bit quantized baseline, prefix KV caching for the top 20% of prefixes, 2s latency SLO for interactive routes with batch size capped at 8.
- Commercial ask: 3-month pilot at $X usage credit + $Y one-time onboarding credit; flexibility to convert into a 12-month reserved capacity commit with an above-the-line credit if we move forward.

Action items I promised:
1) A short matrix showing cost delta (hosted per-token) across quantization levels (fp16, int8, int4) + cache hit assumptions. See tab "Cost Scenarios" in the workbook.
2) A recommended fallback policy for high concurrency windows so your app keeps responding if we run out of burst capacity.
3) A one-page summary you can share with procurement highlighting security points and SLA language.

Notes / questions for you:
- Which procurement timeline are you targeting? (E.g., sign by end of May / pilot starts June 1).
- Any hard constraints on on-prem vs hosted? From the workshop it sounded like hosted with VPC peering is fine for the pilot.

Regards,
David Kim
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference

Thanks David — great workshop. Couple quick clarifications from our product/ops folks:

1) On quantization: our model owners are nervous about going below int8 for generation quality. Can you call out the expected delta in hallucination/stop-token behavior between int8 and int4 in the workbook?
2) On caching: the team wants guidance on how prefix cache invalidation interacts with model rollouts. If we flip to a new model version during pilot, what do you recommend for consistency?

Procurement timeline: aiming for a pilot contract in mid-May if the numbers look reasonable. Also — can you share a sample T&Cs addendum for the pilot (data retention, audit logs, and incident notification SLA)?

Peter
VP Product, Lexera Labs

On Tue, Apr 3, 2028 at 10:45 AM David Kim <david.kim@redwood.inference.com> wrote:
> Peter — quick answers inline and attached a short note for procurement (pilot-addendum.pdf).
>
> 1) Int8 vs int4: we included a micro-eval in the workbook (tab: "Quality Sensitivity") showing delta on stop-token rate and a small prompt set. High-level: int8 typically has negligible quality impact for most conversational flows we tested; int4 shows measurable degradation on longer-context summarization and complex instruction-following. If you have a specific eval set we can run it during the pilot.
>
> 2) Cache + rollouts: recommended pattern is a staged cache invalidation—create a new cache namespace per model version and warm it with a small percentage of traffic (canary). That avoids cross-model contamination and gives you deterministic fallbacks if XX% of requests fall back to old model due to errors. Added a short runbook in the deck (slide 10).
>
> Procurement addendum: attached pilot-addendum.pdf (2 pages) with data retention: default 30 days for KV/prefix cache metadata, logs retained 90 days (enterprise options available). Incident SLA and notification windows are in section 3.
>
> Short follow-ups for your team:
> - If you want to lock a marginal per-token rate for int8, we can draft a 6-month commit proposal with a blended credit.
> - If on-prem is required at pilot scale we need to scope compute lead time (approx 6 weeks for packaged deployment).
>
> Best,
> David
>
> Attachment: pilot-addendum.pdf (pilot legal/ops summary)
